title: Study on Photodeformation of Solvent Resistance in Hydrogen-Bonded Cross-Linked Main-Chain Azobenzene Films
content: Hydrogen-bonded main-chain Azobenzene (azo) photoactive polymers have broad application prospects in flexible actuators, optical actuators and other fields. Hydro-gen bonds, as dynamic reversible physical crosslinking points and crystal networks, limit the macro flow of polymer chains in rigid micro regions, and can improve the stability and mechanical strength of materials. In this paper, three kinds of hydrogen bonded main chain azobenzene polyamide ester (PEAs)semi-crystalline polymers with different flexible chain lengths were synthesized by Michael addition polymerization. The mechanical properties and light response time of the flexible chain length on the main chain polymer were explored. Azobenzene oriented films with a strain of 235% were obtained by a simple solution casting/mechanical stretching method, and uniaxially oriented polymer films with high orientation (48.85%) and fast response (5 s under ultraviolet light, 55 s under visible light) were obtained. These films exhibit light induced deformation not only in air, but also in polar solvents such as water, methanol, ethanol, ordinary saline solutions (such as normal saline, 0.9 wt% NaCl) and simulated seawater (3.5 wt% NaCl) The typical application range of photodeformation has been successfully extended from air to polar solvents. After soaking in water/brine for one month, polarized optical microscopy (POM) showed that the brightness and orientation of the texture of the film remained stable (Δ brightness< 5%), the light response time was stable (6 s under UV light, 65 s under visible light), and the retention rate of photoinduced stress was 95%.
